class DivisionRing (K : Type*)
  extends Ring K, DivInvMonoid K, Nontrivial K, NNRatCast K, RatCast K where
  /-- For a nonzero `a`, `a⁻¹` is a right multiplicative inverse. -/
  protected mul_inv_cancel : ∀ (a : K), a ≠ 0 → a * a⁻¹ = 1
  /-- The inverse of `0` is `0` by convention. -/
  protected inv_zero : (0 : K)⁻¹ = 0
  protected nnratCast := NNRat.castRec
  /-- However `NNRat.cast` is defined, it must be equal to `a / b`.

  Do not use this lemma directly. Use `NNRat.cast_def` instead. -/
  protected nnratCast_def (q : ℚ≥0) : (NNRat.cast q : K) = q.num / q.den := by intros; rfl
  /-- Scalar multiplication by a nonnegative rational number.

  Unless there is a risk of a `Module ℚ≥0 _` instance diamond, write `nnqsmul := _`. This will set
  `nnqsmul` to `(NNRat.cast · * ·)` thanks to unification in the default proof of `nnqsmul_def`.

  Do not use directly. Instead use the `•` notation. -/
  protected nnqsmul : ℚ≥0 → K → K
  /-- However `qsmul` is defined, it must be propositionally equal to multiplication by `Rat.cast`.

  Do not use this lemma directly. Use `NNRat.smul_def` instead. -/
  protected nnqsmul_def (q : ℚ≥0) (a : K) : nnqsmul q a = NNRat.cast q * a := by intros; rfl
  protected ratCast := Rat.castRec
  /-- However `Rat.cast q` is defined, it must be propositionally equal to `q.num / q.den`.

  Do not use this lemma directly. Use `Rat.cast_def` instead. -/
  protected ratCast_def (q : ℚ) : (Rat.cast q : K) = q.num / q.den := by intros; rfl
  /-- Scalar multiplication by a rational number.

  Unless there is a risk of a `Module ℚ _` instance diamond, write `qsmul := _`. This will set
  `qsmul` to `(Rat.cast · * ·)` thanks to unification in the default proof of `qsmul_def`.

  Do not use directly. Instead use the `•` notation. -/
  protected qsmul : ℚ → K → K
  /-- However `qsmul` is defined, it must be propositionally equal to multiplication by `Rat.cast`.

  Do not use this lemma directly. Use `Rat.cast_def` instead. -/
  protected qsmul_def (a : ℚ) (x : K) : qsmul a x = Rat.cast a * x := by intros; rfl

declarations.doc:
A module is a generalization of vector spaces to a scalar semiring.
It consists of a scalar semiring `R` and an additive monoid of "vectors" `M`,
connected by a "scalar multiplication" operation `r • x : M`
(where `r : R` and `x : M`) with some natural associativity and
distributivity axioms similar to those on a ring.

@[ext]
class Module (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] extends
  DistribMulAction R M where
  /-- Scalar multiplication distributes over addition from the right. -/
  protected add_smul : ∀ (r s : R) (x : M), (r + s) • x = r • x + s • x
  /-- Scalar multiplication by zero gives zero. -/
  protected zero_smul : ∀ x : M, (0 : R) • x = 0

declarations.doc:
A preorder is a reflexive, transitive relation `≤`.
In a preorder, `a < b` means `a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a`, and `<` is defined this way by default.
You can override this definition to set a better def-eq.

class Preorder (α : Type*) extends LE α, LT α where
  protected le_refl : ∀ a : α, a ≤ a
  protected le_trans : ∀ a b c : α, a ≤ b → b ≤ c → a ≤ c
  lt := fun a b => a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a
  protected lt_iff_le_not_ge : ∀ a b : α, a < b ↔ a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a := by intros; rfl

declarations.doc:
A linear order is reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric and total relation `≤`.
We assume that every linear ordered type has decidable `(≤)`, `(<)`, and `(=)`.
declarations.source:
class LinearOrder (α : Type*) extends PartialOrder α, Min α, Max α, Ord α where
  /-- A linear order is total. -/
  protected le_total (a b : α) : a ≤ b ∨ b ≤ a
  /-- In a linearly ordered type, we assume the order relations are all decidable. -/
  toDecidableLE : DecidableLE α
  /-- In a linearly ordered type, we assume the order relations are all decidable. -/
  toDecidableEq : DecidableEq α := @decidableEqOfDecidableLE _ _ toDecidableLE
  /-- In a linearly ordered type, we assume the order relations are all decidable. -/
  toDecidableLT : DecidableLT α := @decidableLTOfDecidableLE _ _ toDecidableLE
  min := fun a b => if a ≤ b then a else b
  max := fun a b => if a ≤ b then b else a
  /-- The minimum function is equivalent to the one you get from `minOfLe`. -/
  protected min_def : ∀ a b, min a b = if a ≤ b then a else b := by intros; rfl
  /-- The minimum function is equivalent to the one you get from `maxOfLe`. -/
  protected max_def : ∀ a b, max a b = if a ≤ b then b else a := by intros; rfl
  compare a b := compareOfLessAndEq a b
  /-- Comparison via `compare` is equal to the canonical comparison given decidable `<` and `=`. -/
  compare_eq_compareOfLessAndEq : ∀ a b, compare a b = compareOfLessAndEq a b := by
    compareOfLessAndEq_rfl

declarations.doc:
A distributive lattice is a lattice that satisfies any of four
equivalent distributive properties (of `sup` over `inf` or `inf` over `sup`,
on the left or right).

The definition here chooses `le_sup_inf`: `(x ⊔ y) ⊓ (x ⊔ z) ≤ x ⊔ (y ⊓ z)`. To prove distributivity
from the dual law, use `DistribLattice.ofInfSupLe`.

A classic example of a distributive lattice
is the lattice of subsets of a set, and in fact this example is
generic in the sense that every distributive lattice is realizable
as a sublattice of a powerset lattice.
declarations.source:
class DistribLattice (α) extends Lattice α where
  /-- The infimum distributes over the supremum -/
  protected le_sup_inf : ∀ x y z : α, (x ⊔ y) ⊓ (x ⊔ z) ≤ x ⊔ y ⊓ z
declarations.dedukti: DistribLattice__structure : (G : Set) -> (h : Proof (Lattice G)) -> (le_sup_inf : Proof (forall G (x => forall G (y => forall G (z => Leq (latticeInf (latticeSup x y) (latticeSup x z)) (latticeSup x (latticeInf y z))))))) -> Structure.

readings.Eng: A distributive lattice is a lattice $G$ such that for all elements $x$, $y$ and $z$ of $G$, $\latticeInfMACRoJJ {(\latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{y})}{(\latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{z})}\leq \latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{(\latticeInfMACRoJJ {y}{z})}$.
readings.Fre: Un treillis distributif est un treillis $G$ tel que pour tous les éléments $x$, $y$ et $z$ de $G$, $\latticeInfMACRoJJ {(\latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{y})}{(\latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{z})}\leq \latticeSupMACRoJI {x}{(\latticeInfMACRoJJ {y}{z})}$.
readings.Cze: Distributivní svaz je svaz $G$ takový, že pro všechny prvky $x$, $y$ a $z$ z $G$, průsek spojení $x$ a $y$ a spojení $x$ a $z$ je menší nebo rovný než spojení $x$ a průseku $y$ a $z$.
readings.formula: $G \in \mathrm{Set} , [AppPredicateFormula] , \forall x \in G . \forall y \in G . \forall z \in G . \latticeInfMACRoJV {(\latticeSupMACRoJU {x}{y})}{(\latticeSupMACRoJU {x}{z})}\leq \latticeSupMACRoJU {x}{(\latticeInfMACRoJV {y}{z})}\vdash \mathrm{Structure}$

declarations.doc:
`Nat.Prime p` means that `p` is a prime number, that is, a natural number
at least 2 whose only divisors are `p` and `1`.
The theorem `Nat.prime_def` witnesses this description of a prime number.

declarations.dedukti:
def Nat__Prime : (p : Elem Nat) -> Prop :=

declarations.statement: ∀ {p : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p ↔ 2 ≤ p ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ), m ∣ p → m = 1 ∨ m = p
declarations.dedukti: Nat__prime_def : (p : Elem Nat) -> Proof (iff (prime p) (and (Leq 2 p) (forall Nat (m => if (divide m p) (or (Eq m 1) (Eq m p)))))).

Eng: \hspace*{1.5em}Assume that $2 \leq p$ and for all elements $m$ of $\Natural$, if $\divides {m}{p}$, then $m = 1$ or $m = p$.
It is enough to show that $p$ is prime.
\hspace*{1.5em}It is enough to show that for all elements $a$ and $b$ of $\Natural$, if $p = a \times b$, then $a$ is a unit or $b$ is a unit.
\hspace*{1.5em}It is enough to show that $a = 1$ or $b = 1$.

Il suffit de montrer que $p$ est premier.
\hspace*{1.5em}Il suffit de montrer que pour tous les éléments $a$ et $b$ de $\Natural$, si $p = a \times b$, alors $a$ est une unité ou $b$ est une unité.
TACTIC:rw [← mul_right_inj' (Nat.ne_zero_of_lt h1), ← hab, ← hab, mul_one]

\hspace*{1.5em}Stačí ukázat, že pro všechny prvky $a$ a $b$ z $\Natural$, jestliže $p = a \times b$, pak $a$ je jednotka nebo $b$ je jednotka.

declarations.doc:
If `n < k * k`, then `minFacAux n k = n`, if `k | n`, then `minFacAux n k = k`.
Otherwise, `minFacAux n k = minFacAux n (k+2)` using well-founded recursion.
If `n` is odd and `1 < n`, then `minFacAux n 3` is the smallest prime factor of `n`.

This definition is by well-founded recursion, so `rfl` or `decide` cannot be used.
One can use `norm_num` to prove `Nat.prime n` for small `n`.

declarations.doc:
The factorization of `m` in `n` is the number of positive natural numbers `i` such that `m ^ i`
divides `n`. Note `m` is prime. This set is expressed by filtering `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound
greater than `log m n`.
declarations.statement: ∀ {b m n : ℕ}, Nat.Prime m → 0 < n → n < m ^ b → n.factorization m = {i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 b | m ^ i ∣ n}.card
declarations.dedukti: Nat__factorization_eq_card_pow_dvd_of_lt : (b : Elem Nat) -> (m : Elem Nat) -> (n : Elem Nat) -> (hm : Proof (prime m)) -> (hn : Proof (Lt 0 n)) -> (hb : Proof (Lt n (pow m b))) -> Proof (Eq (Nat__factorization__app n m) (Finset__card Nat (Finset__filter Nat (i => divide (pow m i) n) (Finset__Ico Nat 1 b)))).

readings.Eng: Let $b , m , n \in \Natural$ such that $m$ is prime and $0 < n < m ^ {b}$. Then $\NatfactorizationappMACRoDF {n}{m}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {(\FinsetFilter {i}{(\divides {(m ^ {i})}{n})}{(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {1}{b})})}$.
readings.Fre: Soit $b , m , n \in \Natural$ tel que $m$ est premier et $0 < n < m ^ {b}$. Alors $\NatfactorizationappMACRoDF {n}{m}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {(\FinsetFilter {i}{(\divides {(m ^ {i})}{n})}{(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {1}{b})})}$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $b , m , n \in \Natural$ takový, že $m$ je prvočíselné a $0 < n < m ^ {b}$. Tedy násobnost $m$ v $n$ je rovná mohutnosti $\FinsetFilter {i}{(\divides {(m ^ {i})}{n})}{(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {1}{b})}$.

declarations.doc:
If `p` is a prime factor of `a` then the power of `p` in `a` is the same that in `a * b`,
for any `b` coprime to `a`.
declarations.statement: ∀ {p a b : ℕ}, a.Coprime b → p ∈ a.primeFactorsList → (a * b).factorization p = a.factorization p

we can evaluate `f n` by evaluating `f` at `p ^ k` over the factorization of `n`

    f 0 = 1 → f 1 = 1 → f n = n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k)

declarations.doc:
Flooring root of a natural number. This divides the valuation of every prime number rounding
down.

Eg if `n = 2`, `a = 2^3 * 3^2 * 5`, then `floorRoot n a = 2 * 3`.

In order theory terms, this is the upper or right adjoint of the map `a ↦ a ^ n : ℕ → ℕ` where `ℕ`
is ordered by divisibility.

To ensure that the adjunction (`Nat.pow_dvd_iff_dvd_floorRoot`) holds in as many cases as possible,
we special-case the following values:
* `floorRoot 0 a = 0`
* `floorRoot n 0 = 0`

declarations.doc:
Ceiling root of a natural number. This divides the valuation of every prime number rounding up.

Eg if `n = 3`, `a = 2^4 * 3^2 * 5`, then `ceilRoot n a = 2^2 * 3 * 5`.

In order theory terms, this is the lower or left adjoint of the map `a ↦ a ^ n : ℕ → ℕ` where `ℕ`
is ordered by divisibility.

To ensure that the adjunction (`Nat.dvd_pow_iff_ceilRoot_dvd`) holds in as many cases as possible,
we special-case the following values:
* `ceilRoot 0 a = 0` (this one is not strictly necessary)
* `ceilRoot n 0 = 0`
declarations.statement: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
declarations.dedukti:
def Nat__ceilRoot : (n : Elem Nat) -> (a : Elem Nat) -> Elem Nat :=
  n => a => ite Nat (or (Eq n 0) (Eq a 0)) 0 (Finsupp__prod Nat Nat Nat (Nat__factorization a) (p => k => pow p (div (minus (plus k n) 1) n))).

declarations.doc:
factorial notation `(n)!` for `Nat.factorial n`.
In Lean, names can end with exclamation marks (e.g. `List.get!`), so you cannot write
`n!` in Lean, but must write `(n)!` or `n !` instead. The former is preferred, since
Lean can confuse the `!` in `n !` as the (prefix) Boolean negation operation in some
cases.
For numerals the parentheses are not required, so e.g. `0!` or `1!` work fine.

declarations.statement:

declarations.doc: The **binomial theorem**
declarations.statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (x y : R) (n : ℕ),
  (x + y) ^ n = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), x ^ m * y ^ (n - m) * ↑(n.choose m)

def add_pow : (R : Set) -> (_ : Proof (CommSemiring R)) -> (x1 : Elem R) -> (y : Elem R) -> (n : Elem Nat) -> Proof (Eqt R (pow (plus x1 y) n) (Finset__sum Nat R (Finset__range (plus n 1)) (m => times (times (pow x1 m) (pow y (minus n m))) (Nat__cast R (Nat__choose n m))))) :=
  R => x => x1 => y => n => Commute__add_pow R x1 y (Commute__all R x1 y) n.

declarations.doc:
**Zhu Shijie's identity** aka hockey-stick identity, version with `range`.
Summing `(i + k).choose k` for `i ∈ [0, n]` gives `(n + k + 1).choose (k + 1)`.

Combinatorial interpretation: `(i + k).choose k` is the number of decompositions of `[0, i)` in
`k + 1` (possibly empty) intervals (this follows from a stars and bars description). In particular,
`(n + k + 1).choose (k + 1)` corresponds to decomposing `[0, n)` into `k + 2` intervals.
By putting away the last interval (of some length `n - i`),
we have to decompose the remaining interval `[0, i)` into `k + 1` intervals, hence the sum.

The sum of `(n+1).choose i * f i (n+1-i)` can be split into two sums at rank `n`,

  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 2), ↑((n + 1).choose i) * f i (n + 1 - i) =

declarations.doc:
`n : ℕ` is perfect if and only the sum of the proper divisors of `n` is `n` and `n`
is positive.
declarations.statement: ℕ → Prop
declarations.dedukti:
def Nat__Perfect : (n : Elem Nat) -> Prop :=
  n => and (Eq (Finset__sum Nat Nat (Nat__properDivisors n) (i => i)) n) (Lt 0 n).

readings.Eng: Let $n \in \Natural$. Then $n$ is perfect, if $\FinsetSum {\mathrm{Nat\_\_properDivisors} (n)}{i}{i}= n$ and $0 < n$.
readings.Fre: Soit $n \in \Natural$. Alors $n$ est parfait si $\FinsetSum {\mathrm{Nat\_\_properDivisors} (n)}{i}{i}= n$ et $0 < n$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $n \in \Natural$. Tedy $n$ je dokonalé, jestliže $\FinsetSum {\mathrm{Nat\_\_properDivisors} (n)}{i}{i}= n$ a $0 < n$.

declarations.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → (n.Perfect ↔ ∑ i ∈ n.properDivisors, i = n)
declarations.dedukti:
def Nat__perfect_iff_sum_properDivisors : (n : Elem Nat) -> (h : Proof (Lt 0 n)) -> Proof (iff (Nat__Perfect n) (Eq (Finset__sum Nat Nat (Nat__properDivisors n) (i => i)) n)) :=
  n => h => and_iff_left (Lt 0 n) (Eq (Finset__sum Nat Nat (Nat__properDivisors n) (i => i)) n) h.

declarations.statement: ∀ {p : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → ∀ (k : ℕ) {x : ℕ}, x ∈ (p ^ k).divisors ↔ ∃ j ≤ k, x = p ^ j

readings.Eng: Let $p , k , x \in \Natural$ such that $p$ is prime. Then $x$ is an element of the set of divisors of $p ^ {k}$, if and only if there exists a natural number $j$, such that $j \leq k$ and $x = p ^ {j}$.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a set. Let $s$ and $t$ be finite sets of $X$ such that $s$ is disjoint to $t$. Then the disjoint union of $s$ and $t$ is equal to $\UnionunionMACRoDY {s}{t}$.
readings.Fre: Soit $X$ un ensemble. Soient $s$ et $t$ des ensembles finis de $X$ tels que $s$ soit disjoint à $t$. Alors la réunion disjointe de $s$ et $t$ est égale à $\UnionunionMACRoDY {s}{t}$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ je množina. Nechť $s$ a $t$ je konečná množina $X$ taková, že $s$ je disjunktní do $t$. Tedy disjunktní sjednocení $s$ a $t$ je rovné sjednocení $s$ a $t$.

declarations.doc:
Given a bijection from a finite set `s` to a finite set `t`, the cardinalities of `s` and `t`
are equal.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection,
rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the
domain, rather than being a non-dependent function.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (i : (a : α) → a ∈ s → β),
  (∀ (a : α) (ha : a ∈ s), i a ha ∈ t) →
    (∀ (a₁ : α) (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ s) (a₂ : α) (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ s), i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂) →
      (∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a, ∃ (ha : a ∈ s), i a ha = b) → s.card = t.card
declarations.dedukti: Finset__card_bij : (X : Set) -> (Y : Set) -> (s : Elem (Finset X)) -> (t : Elem (Finset Y)) -> (i : ((a2 : Elem X) -> Proof (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s a2) -> Y)) -> (hi : Proof (forall X (a1 => forall (Proof (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s a1)) (ha1 => Membership__mem Y (Finset Y) t (i a1 ha1))))) -> (i_inj : Proof (forall X (x => forall (Proof (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s x)) (h1 => forall X (x1 => forall (Proof (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s x1)) (h2 => if (Eqt Y (i x h1) (i x1 h2)) (Eqt X x x1))))))) -> (i_surj : Proof (forall Y (b => if (Membership__mem Y (Finset Y) t b) (exists X (a => exists (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s a) (ha => Eqt Y (i a ha) b)))))) -> Proof (Eq (Finset__card X s) (Finset__card Y t)).

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $t$ be a finite set of $Y$. Let $i$ be a function from elements $a_{2}$ of $X$ and elements of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{2}})$ to elements of $Y$ such that for all elements $a_{1}$ of $X$, for all elements $\mathrm{ha1}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{1}})$, $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {t}{i (a_{1} , \mathrm{ha1})}$, for all elements $x$ of $X$, for all elements $h_{1}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{x})$, for all elements $x_{1}$ of $X$, for all elements $h_{2}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{x_{1}})$, if $i (x , h_{1})$ is equal to $i (x_{1} , h_{2})$, then $x$ is equal to $x_{1}$ and for all elements $b$ of $Y$, if $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {t}{b}$, then there exists an element $a$ of $X$, such that there exists an element $\mathrm{ha}$ of $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a}$, such that $\EqtMACRoDE {i (a , \mathrm{ha})}{b}$. Then $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.
readings.Fre: Soient $X$ et $Y$ des ensembles. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $X$. Soit $t$ un ensemble fini de $Y$. Soit $i$ une fonction des éléments $a_{2}$ de $X$ et des éléments de $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{2}})$ à des éléments de $Y$ telle que pour tous les éléments $a_{1}$ de $X$, pour tous les éléments $\mathrm{ha1}$ de $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{1}})$, $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {t}{i (a_{1} , \mathrm{ha1})}$, pour tous les éléments $x$ de $X$, pour tous les éléments $h_{1}$ de $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{x})$, pour tous les éléments $x_{1}$ de $X$, pour tous les éléments $h_{2}$ de $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{x_{1}})$, si $i (x , h_{1})$ est égal à $i (x_{1} , h_{2})$, alors $x$ soit égal à $x_{1}$ et pour tous les éléments $b$ de $Y$, si $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {t}{b}$, alors il existe un élément $a$ de $X$ tel que il existe un élément $\mathrm{ha}$ de $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a}$ tel que $\EqtMACRoDE {i (a , \mathrm{ha})}{b}$. Alors $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.

  Set.MapsTo i ↑s ↑t → Set.MapsTo j ↑t ↑s → Set.LeftInvOn j i ↑s → Set.RightInvOn j i ↑t → s.card = t.card
declarations.dedukti:
def Finset__card_nbij' : (X : Set) -> (Y : Set) -> (s : Elem (Finset X)) -> (t : Elem (Finset Y)) -> (i : (Elem X -> Y)) -> (j : (Elem Y -> X)) -> (hi : Proof (Set__MapsTo X Y i (SetLike__coe (Finset X) X s) (SetLike__coe (Finset Y) Y t))) -> (hj : Proof (Set__MapsTo Y X j (SetLike__coe (Finset Y) Y t) (SetLike__coe (Finset X) X s))) -> (left_inv : Proof (Set__LeftInvOn X Y j i (SetLike__coe (Finset X) X s))) -> (right_inv : Proof (Set__RightInvOn X Y j i (SetLike__coe (Finset Y) Y t))) -> Proof (Eq (Finset__card X s) (Finset__card Y t)) :=
  X => Y => s => t => i => j => hi => hj => left_inv => right_inv => Finset__card_bij' X Y s t (a => h => i a) (b => h1 => j b) hi hj left_inv right_inv.

declarations.doc:
Specialization of `Finset.card_nbij'` that automatically fills in most arguments.

See `Fintype.card_equiv` for the version where `s` and `t` are `univ`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (e : α ≃ β),
  (∀ (i : α), i ∈ s ↔ e i ∈ t) → s.card = t.card

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $t$ be a finite set of $Y$. Let $e \in \EquivMACRoEB {X}{Y}$ such that for all elements $i$ of $X$, $i$ is an element of $s$, if and only if $e (i)$ is an element of $t$. Then $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.
readings.Fre: Soient $X$ et $Y$ des ensembles. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $X$. Soit $t$ un ensemble fini de $Y$. Soit $e \in \EquivMACRoEB {X}{Y}$ tel que pour tous les éléments $i$ de $X$, $i$ est un élément de $s$ si et seulement si $e (i)$ est un élément de $t$. Alors $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ a $Y$ je množina. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $X$. Nechť $t$ je konečná množina $Y$. Nechť $e \in \EquivMACRoEB {X}{Y}$ takový, že pro všechny prvky $i$ z $X$, $i$ je element $s$, právě tehdy, když $e (i)$ je element $t$. Tedy mohutnost $s$ je rovná mohutnosti $t$.

declarations.doc:
Specialization of `Finset.card_nbij` that automatically fills in most arguments.

See `Fintype.card_bijective` for the version where `s` and `t` are `univ`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (e : α → β),
  Function.Bijective e → (∀ (i : α), i ∈ s ↔ e i ∈ t) → s.card = t.card
declarations.dedukti:
def Finset__card_bijective : (X : Set) -> (Y : Set) -> (s : Elem (Finset X)) -> (t : Elem (Finset Y)) -> (e : (Elem X -> Y)) -> (he : Proof (Function__Bijective X Y e)) -> (hst : Proof (forall X (i => iff (Membership__mem X (Finset X) s i) (Membership__mem Y (Finset Y) t (e i))))) -> Proof (Eq (Finset__card X s) (Finset__card Y t)) :=
  X => Y => s => t => e => he => hst => Finset__card_equiv X Y s t (Equiv__ofBijective X Y e he) hst.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $t$ be a finite set of $Y$. Let $e$ be a function from elements of $X$ to elements of $Y$ such that $e$ is bijective and for all elements $i$ of $X$, $i$ is an element of $s$, if and only if $e (i)$ is an element of $t$. Then $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.

Nechť $e$ je funkce z prvků z $X$ do prvků z $Y$ taková, že $e$ je bijektivní a pro všechny prvky $i$ z $X$, $i$ je element $s$, právě tehdy, když $e (i)$ je element $t$. Then there exists an element $x$ of $X$, such that $x$ is an element of $s$ and there exists an element $y$ of $X$, such that $y$ is an element of $s$, $x \neq y$ and $f (x)$ is equal to $f (y)$.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a set. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $n \in \Natural$. Let $f$ be a function from natural numbers to elements of $X$ such that for all natural numbers $i_{1}$, if $i_{1} < n$, then $f (i_{1})$ is an element of $s$ and for all natural numbers $i$, if $i < n$, then for all natural numbers $j$, if $j < n$, then if $f (i)$ is equal to $f (j)$, then $i = j$. Then $n \leq \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}$.

declarations.doc:
Given an injective map `f` from a finite set `s` to another finite set `t`, if `t` is no larger
than `s`, then `f` is surjective to `t` when restricted to `s`.
See `Finset.surj_on_of_inj_on_of_card_le` for the version where `f` is a dependent function.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (f : α → β),
  Set.MapsTo f ↑s ↑t → Set.InjOn f ↑s → t.card ≤ s.card → Set.SurjOn f ↑s ↑t

Soit $t$ un ensemble fini de $Y$ tel que $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}\leq \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$. Alors $\FinsetimageMACRoHR {f}{s}$ est égal à $t$ si et seulement si $f$ est une bijection de $s$ à $t$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ a $Y$ je množina. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $X$. Nechť $f$ je funkce z prvků z $X$ do prvků z $Y$. Nechť $t$ je konečná množina $Y$ taková, že $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}\leq \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$. Tedy obraz $s$ pod $f$ je rovný $t$, právě tehdy, když $f$ je bijekce z $s$ do $t$.

declarations.doc:
Suppose that, given objects defined on all strict subsets of any finset `s`, one knows how to
define an object on `s`. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets, starting from
the empty set and iterating. This can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.

declarations.doc:
To prove a proposition for an arbitrary `Finset α`,
it suffices to prove that for any `S : Finset α`, the following is true:
the property is true for S with any element `s` removed, then the property holds for `S`.

This is a weaker version of `Finset.strongInduction`.
But it can be more precise when the induction argument
only requires removing single elements at a time.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {p : Finset α → Prop},
  (∀ (S : Finset α), (∀ s ∈ S, p (S.erase s)) → p S) → ∀ (S : Finset α), p S
declarations.dedukti:
def Finset__eraseInduction : (X : Set) -> (p : (Elem (Finset X) -> Prop)) -> (H : Proof (forall (Finset X) (S1 => if (forall X (s => if (Membership__mem X (Finset X) S1 s) (p (Finset__erase X S1 s)))) (p S1)))) -> (S : Elem (Finset X)) -> Proof (p S) :=
  X => p => H => S => Finset__strongInduction X p (forallI (Finset X) (S1 => if (forall (Finset X) (t2 => if (HasSSubset__SSubset (Finset X) t2 S1) (p t2))) (p S1)) (S1 => ifI (forall (Finset X) (t1 => if (HasSSubset__SSubset (Finset X) t1 S1) (p t1))) (p S1) (ih => ifE (forall X (s1 => if (Membership__mem X (Finset X) S1 s1) (p (Finset__erase X S1 s1)))) (p S1) (forallE (Finset X) (S2 => if (forall X (s => if (Membership__mem X (Finset X) S2 s) (p (Finset__erase X S2 s)))) (p S2)) H S1) (forallI X (x1 => if (Membership__mem X (Finset X) S1 x1) (p (Finset__erase X S1 x1))) (x1 => ifI (Membership__mem X (Finset X) S1 x1) (p (Finset__erase X S1 x1)) (hs => ifE (HasSSubset__SSubset (Finset X) (Finset__erase X S1 x1) S1) (p (Finset__erase X S1 x1)) (forallE (Finset X) (t => if (HasSSubset__SSubset (Finset X) t S1) (p t)) ih (Finset__erase X S1 x1)) (Finset__erase_ssubset X x1 S1 hs))))))) S.

declarations.doc:
Given a function `f` which sends the finite set `s` to itself, the sequence of images of `s` under
iterates of `f` is eventually constant. Furthermore, the sequence of images stabilises in fewer
than `#s` steps.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {s : Finset α},
  Set.MapsTo f ↑s ↑s → s.Nonempty → ∃ n < s.card, ∀ (m : ℕ), n ≤ m → Finset.image f^[m] s = Finset.image f^[n] s
declarations.dedukti: Finset__image_iterate_stabilises_lt_card : (X : Set) -> (f : (Elem X -> X)) -> (s : Elem (Finset X)) -> (hs : Proof (Set__MapsTo X X f (SetLike__coe (Finset X) X s) (SetLike__coe (Finset X) X s))) -> (h : Proof (Finset__Nonempty X s)) -> Proof (exists Nat (n => and (Lt n (Finset__card X s)) (forall Nat (m => if (Leq n m) (Eqt (Finset X) (Finset__image X X (Nat__iterate X f m) s) (Finset__image X X (Nat__iterate X f n) s)))))).

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a finite type. Let $s \in \wp X$ such that the set of elements of $s$ is a finite type and the set of elements of the complement of $s$ is a finite type. declarations.doc:
Given that `α ⊕ β` is a fintype, `α` is also a fintype. This is non-computable as it uses
that `Sum.inl` is an injection, but there's no clear inverse if `α` is empty.
declarations.statement: {α : Type u_3} → {β : Type u_4} → [Fintype (α ⊕ β)] → Fintype α
declarations.dedukti:

Eng: \hspace*{1.5em}There exists a function $\mathrm{finv}$ from elements of $X$ to elements of $X$, such that $\mathrm{finv}$ is a left inverse of $f$.

\hspace*{1.5em}Il existe une fonction $\mathrm{finv}$ des éléments de $X$ à des éléments de $X$ tel que $\mathrm{finv}$ soit un inverse à gauche de $f$.

$f$ je injektivní, právě tehdy, když $f$ je surjektivní.

declarations.doc:
A custom induction principle for fintypes. The base case is a subsingleton type,
and the induction step is for non-trivial types, and one can assume the hypothesis for
smaller types (via `Fintype.card`).

The major premise is `Fintype α`, so to use this with the `induction` tactic you have to give a name
to that instance and use that name.
declarations.statement:
∀ {P : (α : Type u_3) → [Fintype α] → Prop} (α : Type u_3) [inst : Fintype α],
  (∀ (α : Type u_3) [inst : Fintype α] [Subsingleton α], P α) →
    (∀ (α : Type u_3) [inst : Fintype α] [Nontrivial α],
        (∀ (β : Type u_3) [inst_2 : Fintype β], Fintype.card β < Fintype.card α → P β) → P α) →
      P α

readings.Eng: Let $P$ be a function from sets $X_{3}$ and elements of $\mathrm{Proof}$ applied to the proposition that $X_{3}$ is a finite type to propositions. Let $X$ be a finite type. Assume that for all sets $X_{2}$, for all elements $x_{3}$ of $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{2})$, if $X_{2}$ is a subsingleton, then $P (X_{2} , x_{3})$. Assume that for all sets $X_{1}$, for all elements $x_{1}$ of $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{1})$, if $X_{1}$ is nontrivial, then if for all sets $Y$, for all elements $x_{2}$ of $\mathrm{Fintype} (Y)$, if $\FintypecardMACRoIR {Y}< \FintypecardMACRoIR {X_{1}}$, then $P (Y , x_{2})$, then $P (X_{1} , x_{1})$. Then $P (X , x)$.
readings.Fre: Soit $P$ une fonction des ensembles $X_{3}$ et des éléments de $\mathrm{Proof}$ appliqué à la proposition que $X_{3}$ est un type fini à des propositions. Soit $X$ un type fini. Supposons que pour tous les ensembles $X_{2}$, pour tous les éléments $x_{3}$ de $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{2})$, si $X_{2}$ est un sous-singleton, alors $P (X_{2} , x_{3})$. Supposons que pour tous les ensembles $X_{1}$, pour tous les éléments $x_{1}$ de $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{1})$, si $X_{1}$ est non trivial, alors si pour tous les ensembles $Y$, pour tous les éléments $x_{2}$ de $\mathrm{Fintype} (Y)$, si $\FintypecardMACRoIR {Y}< \FintypecardMACRoIR {X_{1}}$, alors $P (Y , x_{2})$, alors $P (X_{1} , x_{1})$. Alors $P (X , x)$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $P$ je funkce ze množin $X_{3}$ a prvků z $\mathrm{Proof}$ aplikovaný na výrok že $X_{3}$ je konečný typ do výroků. Nechť $X$ je konečný typ. Předpokládejme, že pro všechny množiny $X_{2}$, pro všechny prvky $x_{3}$ z $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{2})$, jestliže $X_{2}$ je subsingleton, pak $P (X_{2} , x_{3})$. Předpokládejme, že pro všechny množiny $X_{1}$, pro všechny prvky $x_{1}$ z $\mathrm{Fintype} (X_{1})$, jestliže $X_{1}$ je netriviální, pak jestliže pro všechny množiny $Y$, pro všechny prvky $x_{2}$ z $\mathrm{Fintype} (Y)$, jestliže mohutnost $Y$ je menší než mohutnost $X_{1}$, pak $P (Y , x_{2})$, pak $P (X_{1} , x_{1})$. Tedy $P (X , x)$.

Let $p$ be a function from elements of $I$ to propositions such that for all elements $x_{5}$ of $I$, if $x_{5}$ is an element of $s$, then if $f (x_{5})\neq 0$, then $p (x_{5})$. Then $\FinsetSum {(\FinsetFilter {x_{2}}{p (x_{2})}{s})}{x_{3}}{f (x_{3})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {s}{x_{4}}{f (x_{4})}$.

declarations.doc:
The product of a function `g` defined only on a set `s` is equal to
the product of a function `f` defined everywhere,
as long as `f` and `g` agree on `s`, and `f = 1` off `s`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} [inst : CommMonoid M] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] (s : Set ι)
  [inst_2 : DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ s] (f : ι → M) (g : ↑s → M),
  (∀ (x : ι) (hx : x ∈ s), f x = g ⟨x, hx⟩) → (∀ x ∉ s, f x = 1) → ∏ i, f i = ∏ i, g i

Assume that for all elements $x_{3}$ of $I$, if $x_{3}$ is not an element of $s$, then $f (x_{3})$ is equal to $1$. declarations.doc:
For any product along `{0, ..., n - 1}` of a commutative-monoid-valued function, we can verify
that it's equal to a different function just by checking ratios of adjacent terms up to `n`.

This is a multiplicative discrete analogue of the fundamental theorem of calculus.
declarations.statement:
∀ {M : Type u_4} [inst : CommMonoid M] (f s : ℕ → M),
  s 0 = 1 → ∀ (n : ℕ), (∀ k < n, s (k + 1) = s k * f k) → ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, f k = s n

Let $n \in \Natural$ such that for all natural numbers $k_{1}$, if $k_{1} < n$, then $s (k_{1} + 1)$ is equal to $s (k_{1})\times f (k_{1})$. Then $\FinsetProd {\FinsetrangeMACRoDK {n}}{k}{f (k)}$ is equal to $s (n)$.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $I$ to natural numbers. Let $a \in M$. Then $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{a})}$ is equal to $\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {(\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{f (i_{1})})}{a}$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $I$. Soit $f$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des nombres naturels. Soit $a \in M$. Alors $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{a})}$ est égal à $\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {(\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{f (i_{1})})}{a}$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $I$. Nechť $f$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do přirozených čísl. Nechť $a \in M$. Tedy $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{a})}$ je rovné $\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {(\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{f (i_{1})})}{a}$.
readings.formula: $I , M \in \mathrm{Set} , [AppPredicateFormula] , s \in \mathrm{Finset} (I), f \in I \rightarrow \Natural , a \in M \vdash \EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i)}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{f (i_{1})})}{a}}$

Eng: \hspace*{1.5em}To prove that for all elements $x_{2}$ of $I$, for all finite sets $x_{10}$ of $I$, for all elements $h_{5}$ of $\mathrm{Proof}$ applied to the proposition that it is not the case that $\MembershipmemMACRoDX {x_{10}}{x_{2}}$, if $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{10}}{i_{40}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{40})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{10}}{i_{41}}{f (i_{41})})}{a}}$, then $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{10}})}{i_{38}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{38})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{10}})}{i_{39}}{f (i_{39})})}{a}}$, let $x_{2} \in I$.

\hspace*{1.5em}\hspace*{1.5em}To prove that for all finite sets $x_{3}$ of $I$, for all elements $h_{3}$ of $\mathrm{Proof}$ applied to the proposition that it is not the case that $\MembershipmemMACRoDX {x_{3}}{x_{2}}$, if $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{36}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{36})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{37}}{f (i_{37})})}{a}}$, then $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{34}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{34})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{35}}{f (i_{35})})}{a}}$, let $x_{3}$ be a finite set of $I$.

\hspace*{1.5em}\hspace*{1.5em}\hspace*{1.5em}\hspace*{1.5em}To prove that if $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{26}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{26})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{27}}{f (i_{27})})}{a}}$, then $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{28}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{28})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{29}}{f (i_{29})})}{a}}$, assume that $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{26}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{26})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{27}}{f (i_{27})})}{a}}$.

\hspace*{1.5em}For all finite sets $x_{3}$ of $I$, for all elements $h_{3}$ of $\mathrm{Proof}$ applied to the proposition that it is not the case that $\MembershipmemMACRoDX {x_{3}}{x_{2}}$, if $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{36}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{36})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{3}}{i_{37}}{f (i_{37})})}{a}}$, then $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{34}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{34})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{3}})}{i_{35}}{f (i_{35})})}{a}}$.

Fre: \hspace*{1.5em}Pour démontrer que pour tous les éléments $x_{2}$ de $I$, pour tous les ensembles finis $x_{10}$ de $I$, pour tous les éléments $h_{5}$ de $\mathrm{Proof}$ appliqué à la proposition qu'il n'est pas le cas que $\MembershipmemMACRoDX {x_{10}}{x_{2}}$, si $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {x_{10}}{i_{40}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{40})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {x_{10}}{i_{41}}{f (i_{41})})}{a}}$, alors $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{10}})}{i_{38}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {f (i_{38})}{a})}}{\HSMulhSMulMACRoEQ {(\FinsetSum {(\FinsetconsMACRoIX {x_{2}}{x_{10}})}{i_{39}}{f (i_{39})})}{a}}$, soit $x_{2} \in I$.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $M$ be a commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $I$ to natural numbers. Let $a \in M$. Then $\FinsetProd {s}{i}{(a ^ {f (i)})}$ is equal to $a ^ {\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{f (i_{1})}}$.

declarations.doc:
The difference with `Finset.sum_ninvolution` is that the involution is allowed to
use membership of the domain of the sum, rather than being a non-dependent function.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} {s : Finset ι} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] {f : ι → M} (g : (a : ι) → a ∈ s → ι),
  (∀ (a : ι) (ha : a ∈ s), f a + f (g a ha) = 0) →
    (∀ (a : ι) (ha : a ∈ s), f a ≠ 0 → g a ha ≠ a) →
      ∀ (g_mem : ∀ (a : ι) (ha : a ∈ s), g a ha ∈ s), (∀ (a : ι) (ha : a ∈ s), g (g a ha) ⋯ = a) → ∑ x ∈ s, f x = 0

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Let $g$ be a function from elements $a_{4}$ of $I$ and elements of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{4}})$ to elements of $I$ such that for all elements $a_{3}$ of $I$, for all elements $\mathrm{ha3}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{3}})$, $f (a_{3})+ f (g (a_{3} , \mathrm{ha3}))$ is equal to $0$, for all elements $a_{2}$ of $I$, for all elements $\mathrm{ha2}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{2}})$, if $f (a_{2})\neq 0$, then $g (a_{2} , \mathrm{ha2})\neq a_{2}$, for all elements $a_{1}$ of $I$, for all elements $\mathrm{ha1}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a_{1}})$, $g (a_{1} , \mathrm{ha1})$ is an element of $s$ and for all elements $a$ of $I$, for all elements $\mathrm{ha}$ of $\mathrm{Proof} (\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{a})$, $\EqtMACRoDE {g (g (a , \mathrm{ha}), \mathrm{g\_mem} (a , \mathrm{ha}))}{a}$. Then $\EqtMACRoDE {\FinsetSum {s}{x_{1}}{f (x_{1})}}{0}$.

The difference with `Finset.prod_involution` is that the involution is a non-dependent function,
rather than being allowed to use membership of the domain of the product.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $M$ be a commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Let $g$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $I$ such that for all elements $a_{3}$ of $I$, $f (a_{3})\times f (g (a_{3}))$ is equal to $1$, for all elements $a_{2}$ of $I$, if $f (a_{2})\neq 1$, then $g (a_{2})\neq a_{2}$, for all elements $a_{1}$ of $I$, $g (a_{1})$ is an element of $s$ and for all elements $a$ of $I$, $g (g (a))$ is equal to $a$. Then $\FinsetProd {s}{x_{1}}{f (x_{1})}$ is equal to $1$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $I$. Soit $f$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Soit $g$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $I$ telle que pour tous les éléments $a_{3}$ de $I$, $f (a_{3})\times f (g (a_{3}))$ soit égal à $1$, pour tous les éléments $a_{2}$ de $I$, si $f (a_{2})\neq 1$, alors $g (a_{2})\neq a_{2}$, pour tous les éléments $a_{1}$ de $I$, $g (a_{1})$ soit un élément de $s$ et pour tous les éléments $a$ de $I$, $g (g (a))$ soit égal à $a$. Alors $\FinsetProd {s}{x_{1}}{f (x_{1})}$ est égal à $1$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $M$ je komutativní monoid. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $I$. Nechť $f$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Nechť $g$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $I$ taková, že pro všechny prvky $a_{3}$ z $I$, $f (a_{3})\times f (g (a_{3}))$ je rovné $1$, pro všechny prvky $a_{2}$ z $I$, jestliže $f (a_{2})\neq 1$, pak $g (a_{2})\neq a_{2}$, pro všechny prvky $a_{1}$ z $I$, $g (a_{1})$ je element $s$ a pro všechny prvky $a$ z $I$, $g (g (a))$ je rovné $a$. Tedy $\FinsetProd {s}{x_{1}}{f (x_{1})}$ je rovné $1$.

do the terms in that product.

declarations.doc:
If a product is 1 and the function is 1 except possibly at one
point, it is 1 everywhere on the `Finset`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} [inst : CommMonoid M] {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → M} {a : ι},
  ∏ x ∈ s, f x = 1 → (∀ x ∈ s, x ≠ a → f x = 1) → ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 1
declarations.dedukti: Finset__eq_one_of_prod_eq_one : (I : Set) -> (M : Set) -> (_ : Proof (CommMonoid M)) -> (s : Elem (Finset I)) -> (f : (Elem I -> M)) -> (a : Elem I) -> (hp : Proof (Eqt M (Finset__prod I M s (x3 => f x3)) 1)) -> (h1 : Proof (forall I (x2 => if (Membership__mem I (Finset I) s x2) (if (Neq x2 a) (Eqt M (f x2) 1))))) -> (x1 : Elem I) -> (h : Proof (Membership__mem I (Finset I) s x1)) -> Proof (Eqt M (f x1) 1).

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $M$ be a commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Let $a , x_{1} \in I$. Assume that $\FinsetProd {s}{x_{3}}{f (x_{3})}$ is equal to $1$. Assume that for all elements $x_{2}$ of $I$, if $x_{2}$ is an element of $s$, then if $x_{2} \neq a$, then $f (x_{2})$ is equal to $1$. Assume that $x_{1}$ is an element of $s$. declarations.doc:
A telescoping sum along `{0, ..., n-1}` of an `ℕ`-valued function reduces to the difference of
the last and first terms when the function we are summing is monotone.
declarations.statement:

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $M$ be additive commutative monoids such that $X$ is a partially ordered set, $X$ is an ordered cancellative additive monoid, $\mathrm{ExistsAddOfLE} (X)$ and $X$ is a locally finite order. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $X$ to elements of $M$. Let $a , b , c \in X$. Then $\FinsetSum {(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {a}{b})}{x_{4}}{f (x_{4} + c)}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {(a + c)}{(b + c)})}{x_{5}}{f (x_{5})}$.
readings.Fre: Soient $X$ et $M$ des monoïdes commutatifs additifs tels que $X$ soit un ensemble partiellement ordonné, $X$ soit un monoïde additif cancellatif ordonné, $\mathrm{ExistsAddOfLE} (X)$ et $X$ soit un ordre localement fini. Soit $f$ une fonction des éléments de $X$ à des éléments de $M$. Soient $a , b , c \in X$. Alors $\FinsetSum {(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {a}{b})}{x_{4}}{f (x_{4} + c)}$ est égal à $\FinsetSum {(\FinsetIcoMACRoDL {(a + c)}{(b + c)})}{x_{5}}{f (x_{5})}$.

Nechť $f$ je funkce z prvků z $X$ do prvků z $M$. Nechť $a , b , c \in X$. readings.Eng: Let $M$ be a commutative group. Let $n \in \Natural$. Let $a , b \in \FinMACRoHJ {n}$ such that $a \leq b$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $\FinMACRoHJ {(n + 1)}$ to elements of $M$. Then $\FinsetProd {(\FinsetIccMACRoEE {a}{b})}{i}{(\frac{ f (\mathrm{Fin\_\_succ} (i))}{f (\mathrm{Fin\_\_castSucc} (i))})}$ is equal to $\frac{ f (\mathrm{Fin\_\_succ} (b))}{f (\mathrm{Fin\_\_castSucc} (a))}$.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $t$ be a finite set of $Y$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $X$ to elements of $Y$. Let $w$ be a function from elements of $X$ to elements of $M$. Let $b \in M$. Assume that $M$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $M$ is an ordered cancellative additive monoid. Assume that for all elements $a$ of $X$, if $a$ is an element of $s$, then $f (a)$ is an element of $t$. Assume that $\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}}{b}< \FinsetSum {s}{x_{5}}{w (x_{5})}$. Then there exists an element $y$ of $Y$, such that $y$ is an element of $t$ and $b < \FinsetSum {(\FinsetFilter {x_{3}}{(\EqtMACRoDE {f (x_{3})}{y})}{s})}{x_{4}}{w (x_{4})}$.

Supposons que $M$ est un monoïde additif cancellatif ordonné. Supposons que pour tous les éléments $a$ de $X$, si $a$ est un élément de $s$, alors $f (a)$ est un élément de $t$. declarations.doc:
The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version:
if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than `n • b`, they are sorted into some
pigeonholes, and for all but `n` pigeonholes the total weight of the pigeons there is nonpositive,
then for at least one of these `n` pigeonholes, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole
is greater than `b`.

declarations.doc:
The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by heads: there is a pigeonhole with
at least as many pigeons as the ceiling of the average number of pigeons across all pigeonholes.
("The maximum is at least the mean" specialized to integers.)

More formally, given a function between finite sets `s` and `t` and a natural number `n` such that
`#t * n < #s`, there exists `y ∈ t` such that its preimage in `s` has more than `n`
elements.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq β] {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} {f : α → β} {n : ℕ},
  (∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) → t.card * n < s.card → ∃ y ∈ t, n < {x ∈ s | f x = y}.card

at most as many pigeons as the floor of the average number of pigeons across all pigeonholes.  ("The
minimum is at most the mean" specialized to integers.)

declarations.doc:
A version of the pigeonhole principle for set-valued functions.

Given a family of sets `f : α → Finset β` and a choice of indices `s : Finset α`.
Let `k` denote the minimum cardinality of the `f j`s.
If the cardinality of the union `s.biUnion f` is less than `#s`, then
there exists an element `x ∈ s.biUnion f` which is covered by more than `k` of the sets
`f j` (i.e., `k < #{j ∈ s | x ∈ f j}`).

This is a double-counting variant of the pigeonhole principle.
Unlike the classical pigeonhole principle (see
`Finset.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_nsmul_lt_card_of_maps_to`),
this formulation handles a *set-valued* assignment where elements may belong to
multiple sets simultaneously.

declarations.doc:
The strong pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons and pigeonholes.
There is a pigeonhole with at least as many pigeons as
the ceiling of the average number of pigeons across all pigeonholes.
("The maximum is at least the mean" specialized to integers.)

More formally, given a function `f` between finite types `α` and `β` and a number `n` such that
`card β * n < card α`, there exists an element `y : β` such that its preimage has more than `n`
elements.
declarations.statement:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq β] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [inst_2 : Fintype β] (f : α → β) {n : ℕ},
  Fintype.card β * n < Fintype.card α → ∃ y, n < {x | f x = y}.card

def Fintype__exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card : (X : Set) -> (Y : Set) -> (_ : Proof (Fintype X)) -> (_ : Proof (Fintype Y)) -> (f : (Elem X -> Y)) -> (n : Elem Nat) -> (hn : Proof (Lt (times (Fintype__card Y) n) (Fintype__card X))) -> Proof (exists Y (y => Lt n (Finset__card X (Finset__filter X (x3 => Eqt Y (f x3) y) (Finset__univ X))))) :=
  X => Y => x1 => x2 => f => n => hn => Fintype__exists_lt_card_fiber_of_nsmul_lt_card X Y Nat f n hn.

declarations.doc:
A `Basis ι R M` for a module `M` is the type of `ι`-indexed `R`-bases of `M`.

The basis vectors are available as `DFunLike.coe (b : Basis ι R M) : ι → M`.
To turn a linear independent family of vectors spanning `M` into a basis, use `Basis.mk`.
They are internally represented as linear equivs `M ≃ₗ[R] (ι →₀ R)`,
available as `Basis.repr`.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ and $M'$ be additive commutative monoids such that $M$ is a module over $R$ and $M'$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $I$ is finite. Let $b$ be a basis of $M$ over $R$. Let $f$ be a linear equivalence of $M$ and $M'$. Then the equivalence function of the map of $b$ and $f$ is equal to the composition of the inverse of $f$ and the equivalence function of $b$.

Alors la fonction d'équivalences de l'application de $b$ et $f$ est égale à la composition de l'inverse de $f$ et la fonction d'équivalences de $b$.

declarations.doc:
Construct a linear map given the value at the basis, called `Basis.constr b S f` where `b` is
a basis, `f` is the value of the linear map over the elements of the basis, and `S` is an
extra semiring (typically `S = R` or `S = ℕ`).

This definition is parameterized over an extra `Semiring S`,
such that `SMulCommClass R S M'` holds.
If `R` is commutative, you can set `S := R`; if `R` is not commutative,
you can recover an `AddEquiv` by setting `S := ℕ`.
See library note [bundled maps over different rings].

readings.Cze: Nechť $M'$ a $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid. Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ a $S$ je polookruh takový, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. Nechť $b$ je báze $M$ nad $R$. declarations.doc:
If `b` is a basis for `M` and `b'` a basis for `M'`,
and `f`, `g` form a bijection between the basis vectors,
`b.equiv' b' f g hf hg hgf hfg` is a linear equivalence `M ≃ₗ[R] M'`, mapping `b i` to `f (b i)`.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ and $I$ be sets. Let $R$ be a commutative semiring. Let $M$ and $M'$ be additive commutative monoids such that $M$ is a module over $R$ and $M'$ is a module over $R$. Let $b$ be a basis of $M$ over $R$. Let $b'$ be a basis of $M'$ over $R$. Let $f$ be a function from elements of $M$ to elements of $M'$. Let $g$ be a function from elements of $M'$ to elements of $M$. Assume that for all elements $i_{4}$ of $I$, $f (b (i_{4}))$ is an element of the range of $b'$. Assume that for all elements $i_{3}$ of $X$, $g (b' (i_{3}))$ is an element of the range of $b$. Assume that for all elements $i_{2}$ of $I$, $g (f (b (i_{2})))$ is equal to $b (i_{2})$. Assume that for all elements $i_{1}$ of $X$, $f (g (b' (i_{1})))$ is equal to $b' (i_{1})$. Let $i \in X$. Then $\mathrm{LinearEquiv\_\_symm\_\_app}$ applied to the equivalence of $f$ and $g$ and $b' (i)$ is equal to $g (b' (i))$.

readings.Fre: Soient $X$ et $I$ des ensembles. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif tel que $M$ soit un module sur $R$. Soit $b$ une base de $M$ sur $R$. Soit $e \in \EquivMACRoEB {I}{X}$. Alors la somme des coordonnées de la réindexation de $b$ et $e$ est égale à la somme des coordonnées de $b$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ a $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ je polookruh. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid takový, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. Nechť $b$ je báze $M$ nad $R$. Nechť $e \in \EquivMACRoEB {I}{X}$. Tedy suma souřadnic přeindexování $b$ a $e$ je rovná sumě souřadnic $b$.

Eng: It is enough to show that $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app}$ applied to the reindexing of $b$ and $e$ and $x$ is equal to $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app} (b , x)$.
\hspace*{1.5em}By simplification, $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app}$ applied to the reindexing of $b$ and $e$ and $x$ is equal to $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app} (b , x)$.

\hspace*{1.5em}Par simplification, $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app}$ appliqué à la réindexation de $b$ et $e$ et $x$ est égal à $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app} (b , x)$.

\hspace*{1.5em}Zjednodušením, $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app}$ aplikovaný na přeindexování $b$ a $e$ a $x$ je rovné $\mathrm{Module\_\_Basis\_\_sumCoords\_\_app} (b , x)$.

declarations.doc: `LinearIndependent R v` states the family of vectors `v` is linearly independent over `R`.
declarations.statement:
{ι : Type u'} →
  (R : Type u_2) → {M : Type u_4} → (ι → M) → [inst : Semiring R] → [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [Module R M] → Prop

def LinearIndependent : (I : Set) -> (R : Set) -> (M : Set) -> (v : (Elem I -> M)) -> Prop :=
  I => R => M => v => Function__Injective (Finsupp I R) M (Finsupp__linearCombination I M R v).

readings.Eng: Let $I$, $R$ and $M$ be sets. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Then $R$ is independent over $I$, if the linear combination of $R$ and $v$ is injective.
readings.Fre: Soient $I$, $R$ et $M$ des ensembles. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Alors $R$ est indépendant sur $I$ si la combinaison linéaire de $R$ et $v$ est injective.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$, $R$ a $M$ je množina. Nechť $v$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Tedy $R$ je nezávislé nad $I$, jestliže lineární kombinace $R$ a $v$ je injektivní.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Then it is not the case that $v$ is independent on $s$ over $R$, if and only if there exist functions $f$ and $g$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, such that $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {g (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ and there exists an element $i_{2}$ of $I$, such that $i_{2}$ is an element of $s$ and $f (i_{2})\neq g (i_{2})$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $I$. Alors il n'est pas le cas que $v$ soit indépendant sur $s$ sur $R$ si et seulement si il existent des fonctions $f$ et $g$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$ tel que $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ soit égal à $\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {g (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ et il existe un élément $i_{2}$ de $I$ tel que $i_{2}$ soit un élément de $s$ et $f (i_{2})\neq g (i_{2})$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ je polookruh. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid. Nechť $v$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Předpokládejme, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $I$. Tedy není případ že $v$ je nezávislé na $s$ nad $R$, právě tehdy, když existují funkce $f$ a $g$ z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $R$, takový, že $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ je rovné $\FinsetSum {s}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {g (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ a existuje prvek $i_{2}$ z $I$, takový, že $i_{2}$ je element $s$ a $f (i_{2})\neq g (i_{2})$.

declarations.doc:
If the image of a family of vectors under a linear map is linearly independent, then so is
the original family.

  [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_3 : Module R M] [inst_4 : Module R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] M'),
  LinearIndependent R (⇑f ∘ v) → LinearIndependent R v

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ and $M'$ be additive commutative monoids. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $M'$ is a module over $R$. Let $f$ be a linear map of $M$ and $M'$ such that $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {f}{v}$ is independent over $R$. Then $v$ is independent over $R$.

Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Supposons que $M'$ est un module sur $R$. Soit $f$ une application linéaire de $M$ et $M'$ telle que $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {f}{v}$ soit indépendant sur $R$. Alors $v$ est indépendant sur $R$.

declarations.doc:
If `f` is a linear map injective on the span of the range of `v`, then the family `f ∘ v`
is linearly independent if and only if the family `v` is linearly independent.
See `LinearMap.linearIndependent_iff_of_disjoint` for the version with `Set.InjOn` replaced
by `Disjoint` when working over a ring.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u'} {R : Type u_2} {M : Type u_4} {M' : Type u_5} {v : ι → M} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_3 : Module R M] [inst_4 : Module R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] M'),
  Set.InjOn ⇑f ↑(Submodule.span R (Set.range v)) → (LinearIndependent R (⇑f ∘ v) ↔ LinearIndependent R v)

Then $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {f}{v}$ is independent over $R$, if and only if $v$ is independent over $R$.

declarations.doc:
Linear combination representing a vector in the span of linearly independent vectors.

Given a family of linearly independent vectors, we can represent any vector in their span as
a linear combination of these vectors. These are provided by this linear map.
It is simply one direction of `LinearIndependent.linearCombinationEquiv`.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid such that $M$ is a module over $R$. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$ such that $v$ is independent over $R$. Then $i$ is maximal, if and only if for all sets $J$, for all functions $w$ from elements of $J$ to elements of $M$, if $w$ is independent over $R$, then for all functions $j$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $J$, if $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {w}{j}$ is equal to $v$, then $j$ is surjective.

Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$ telle que $v$ soit indépendant sur $R$. Alors $i$ est maximal si et seulement si pour tous les ensembles $J$, pour toutes les fonctions $w$ des éléments de $J$ à des éléments de $M$, si $w$ est indépendant sur $R$, alors pour toutes les fonctions $j$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $J$, si $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {w}{j}$ est égal à $v$, alors $j$ est surjectif.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ je polookruh. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid takový, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $R$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $R$ is a canonically ordered sum. Assume that $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Then $v$ is not independent over $R$, if and only if there exist finite sets $s$ and $t$ of $I$, such that there exists a function $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, such that $s$ is disjoint to $t$, $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ and there exists an element $i_{2}$ of $I$, such that $i_{2}$ is an element of $s$ and $0 < f (i_{2})$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Supposons que $R$ est un ensemble totalement ordonné. Supposons que $R$ est une somme canoniquement ordonnée. Supposons que $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Alors $v$ n'est pas indépendant sur $R$ si et seulement si il existent des ensembles finis $s$ et $t$ de $I$ tel que il existe une fonction $f$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$ tel que $s$ soit disjoint à $t$, $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ soit égal à $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ et il existe un élément $i_{2}$ de $I$ tel que $i_{2}$ soit un élément de $s$ et $0 < f (i_{2})$.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a finite type. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $R$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $R$ is a canonically ordered sum. Assume that $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Then $v$ is independent over $R$, if and only if for all finite sets $t$ of $I$, for all functions $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, if $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {\ComplcomplMACRoFU {t}}{i_{2}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{2})}{v (i_{2})})}$, then for all elements $i$ of $I$, $f (i)$ is equal to $0$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un type fini. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Supposons que $R$ est un ensemble totalement ordonné. Supposons que $R$ est une somme canoniquement ordonnée. Supposons que $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Alors $v$ est indépendant sur $R$ si et seulement si pour tous les ensembles finis $t$ de $I$, pour toutes les fonctions $f$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$, si $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ est égal à $\FinsetSum {\ComplcomplMACRoFU {t}}{i_{2}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{2})}{v (i_{2})})}$, alors pour tous les éléments $i$ de $I$, $f (i)$ est égal à $0$.

Předpokládejme, že $R$ je lineárně uspořádaná množina. Předpokládejme, že $R$ je kanonicky uspořádaná suma. Předpokládejme, že $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Tedy $v$ je nezávislé nad $R$, právě tehdy, když pro všechny konečné množiny $t$  $I$, pro všechny funkce $f$ z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $R$, jestliže $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ je rovné $\FinsetSum {\ComplcomplMACRoFU {t}}{i_{2}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{2})}{v (i_{2})})}$, pak pro všechny prvky $i$ z $I$, $f (i)$ je rovné $0$.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a finite type. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $R$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $R$ is a canonically ordered sum. Assume that $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Then $v$ is not independent over $R$, if and only if there exists a finite set $t$ of $I$, such that there exists a function $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, such that $\FinsetSum {t}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {\ComplcomplMACRoFU {t}}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ and there exists an element $i_{2}$ of $I$, such that $i_{2}$ is an element of $t$ and $0 < f (i_{2})$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un type fini. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Supposons que $R$ est un ensemble totalement ordonné. Supposons que $R$ est une somme canoniquement ordonnée. Supposons que $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Alors $v$ n'est pas indépendant sur $R$ si et seulement si il existe un ensemble fini $t$ de $I$ tel que il existe une fonction $f$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$ tel que $\FinsetSum {t}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ soit égal à $\FinsetSum {\ComplcomplMACRoFU {t}}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ et il existe un élément $i_{2}$ de $I$ tel que $i_{2}$ soit un élément de $t$ et $0 < f (i_{2})$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je konečný typ. Nechť $R$ je polookruh. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid. Nechť $v$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Předpokládejme, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. Assume that $R$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $R$ is a canonically ordered sum. Assume that $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Then $v$ is independent on $s$ over $R$, if and only if for all finite sets $t$ of $I$, if $t$ is a subset of $s$, then for all functions $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, if $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {(\SDiffsdiffMACRoEU {s}{t})}{i_{2}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{2})}{v (i_{2})})}$, then for all elements $i$ of $I$, if $i$ is an element of $s$, then $f (i)$ is equal to $0$.

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a semiring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Assume that $M$ is a module over $R$. Assume that $R$ is a linearly ordered set. Assume that $R$ is a canonically ordered sum. Assume that $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Then it is not the case that $v$ is independent on $s$ over $R$, if and only if there exists a finite set $t$ of $I$, such that $t$ is a subset of $s$ and there exists a function $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, such that $\FinsetSum {t}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {(\SDiffsdiffMACRoEU {s}{t})}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ and there exists an element $i_{2}$ of $I$, such that $i_{2}$ is an element of $t$ and $0 < f (i_{2})$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $R$ un semi-anneau. Soit $M$ un monoïde commutatif additif. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Supposons que $M$ est un module sur $R$. Supposons que $R$ est un ensemble totalement ordonné. Supposons que $R$ est une somme canoniquement ordonnée. Supposons que $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $I$. Alors il n'est pas le cas que $v$ soit indépendant sur $s$ sur $R$ si et seulement si il existe un ensemble fini $t$ de $I$ tel que $\SetSubsetMACRoFR {t}{s}$ et il existe une fonction $f$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$ tel que $\FinsetSum {t}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ soit égal à $\FinsetSum {(\SDiffsdiffMACRoEU {s}{t})}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ et il existe un élément $i_{2}$ de $I$ tel que $i_{2}$ soit un élément de $t$ et $0 < f (i_{2})$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ je polookruh. Nechť $M$ je aditivní komutativní monoid. Nechť $v$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Předpokládejme, že $M$ je modul nad $R$. Předpokládejme, že $R$ je lineárně uspořádaná množina. Předpokládejme, že $R$ je kanonicky uspořádaná suma. Předpokládejme, že $\mathrm{IsCancelAdd} (M)$. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $I$. Tedy není případ že $v$ je nezávislé na $s$ nad $R$, právě tehdy, když existuje konečná množina $t$  $I$, takový, že $t$ je podmnožina $s$ a existuje funkce $f$ z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $R$, takový, že $\FinsetSum {t}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ je rovné $\FinsetSum {(\SDiffsdiffMACRoEU {s}{t})}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ a existuje prvek $i_{2}$ z $I$, takový, že $i_{2}$ je element $t$ a $0 < f (i_{2})$.

declarations.doc:
A version of `linearIndependent_iff` where the linear combination is a `Finset` sum
of a function with support contained in the `Finset`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u'} {R : Type u_2} {M : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M] [inst_2 : Module R M]

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an additive commutative group such that $M$ is a module over $R$. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Let $s$ be a finite set of $I$. Then it is not the case that $v$ is independent on $s$ over $R$, if and only if there exists a function $f$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, such that $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ is equal to $0$ and there exists an element $i_{1}$ of $I$, such that $i_{1}$ is an element of $s$ and $f (i_{1})\neq 0$.

Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $I$. Alors il n'est pas le cas que $v$ soit indépendant sur $s$ sur $R$ si et seulement si il existe une fonction $f$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$ tel que $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ soit égal à $0$ et il existe un élément $i_{1}$ de $I$ tel que $i_{1}$ soit un élément de $s$ et $f (i_{1})\neq 0$.

Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $I$. Tedy není případ že $v$ je nezávislé na $s$ nad $R$, právě tehdy, když existuje funkce $f$ z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $R$, takový, že $\FinsetSum {s}{i}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {f (i)}{v (i)})}$ je rovné $0$ a existuje prvek $i_{1}$ z $I$, takový, že $i_{1}$ je element $s$ a $f (i_{1})\neq 0$.

declarations.doc:
If the kernel of a linear map is disjoint from the span of a family of vectors,
then the family is linearly independent iff it is linearly independent after composing with
the linear map.

  Disjoint (Submodule.span R (Set.range v)) f.ker → (LinearIndependent R (⇑f ∘ v) ↔ LinearIndependent R v)

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ and $M'$ be additive commutative groups such that $M$ is a module over $R$ and $M'$ is a module over $R$. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Let $f$ be a linear map of $M$ and $M'$ such that the span of the range of $v$ is disjoint to the kernel of $f$. Then $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {f}{v}$ is independent over $R$, if and only if $v$ is independent over $R$.
readings.Fre: Soit $I$ un ensemble. Soit $R$ un anneau. Soient $M$ et $M'$ des groupes commutatifs additifs tels que $M$ soit un module sur $R$ et $M'$ soit un module sur $R$. Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Soit $f$ une application linéaire de $M$ et $M'$ telle que l'envergure de l'image de $v$ soit disjointe au noyau de $f$. Alors $\FunctioncompMACRoEM {f}{v}$ est indépendant sur $R$ si et seulement si $v$ est indépendant sur $R$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $I$ je množina. Nechť $R$ je okruh. Nechť $M$ a $M'$ je aditivní komutativní grupa taková, že $M$ je modul nad $R$ a $M'$ je modul nad $R$. Nechť $v$ je funkce z prvků z $I$ do prvků z $M$. Nechť $f$ je lineární zobrazení $M$ a $M'$ takové, že obal rozsahu $v$ je disjunktní do jádra $f$. Tedy kompozice $f$ a $v$ je nezávislá nad $R$, právě tehdy, když $v$ je nezávislé nad $R$.

Eng: Assume that the span of the range of $v$ is disjoint to the kernel of $f$.
The span of the range of $v$ is less than or equal to the span of the range of $v$.
$f$ is injective on the span of the range of $v$.
$\FunctioncompMACRoEV {f}{v}$ is independent over $R$, if and only if $v$ is independent over $R$.
Fre: Supposons que l'envergure de l'image de $v$ est disjointe au noyau de $f$.
L'envergure de l'image de $v$ est inférieure ou égale à l'envergure de l'image de $v$.
$f$ est injectif sur l'envergure de l'image de $v$.
$\FunctioncompMACRoEV {f}{v}$ est indépendant sur $R$ si et seulement si $v$ est indépendant sur $R$.
Cze: Předpokládejme, že obal rozsahu $v$ je disjunktní do jádra $f$.
Obal rozsahu $v$ je menší nebo rovný než obal rozsahu $v$.
$\FunctioncompMACRoEV {f}{v}$ je nezávislé nad $R$, právě tehdy, když $v$ je nezávislé nad $R$.

declarations.doc:
A version of `linearIndepOn_iff` where the linear combination is a `Finset` sum
of a function with support contained in the `Finset`.
declarations.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u'} {R : Type u_2} {s : Set ι} {M : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] {v : ι → M},
  LinearIndepOn R v s ↔
    ∀ (t : Finset ι) (g : ι → R), ↑t ⊆ s → (∀ i ∉ t, g i = 0) → ∑ i ∈ t, g i • v i = 0 → ∀ i ∈ t, g i = 0
declarations.dedukti: linearIndepOn_iff'' : (I : Set) -> (R : Set) -> (s : Elem (powerset I)) -> (M : Set) -> (_ : Proof (Ring R)) -> (_ : Proof (AddCommGroup M)) -> (_ : Proof (Module R M)) -> (v : (Elem I -> M)) -> Proof (iff (LinearIndepOn I R M v s) (forall (Finset I) (t => forall (Elem I -> R) (g => if (Set__Subset I (SetLike__coe (Finset I) I t) s) (if (forall I (i2 => if (not (Membership__mem I (Finset I) t i2)) (Eqt R (g i2) 0))) (if (Eqt M (Finset__sum I M t (i1 => HSMul__hSMul R M M (g i1) (v i1))) 0) (forall I (i => if (Membership__mem I (Finset I) t i) (Eqt R (g i) 0))))))))).

readings.Eng: Let $I$ be a set. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $s \in \wp I$. Let $M$ be an additive commutative group such that $M$ is a module over $R$. Let $v$ be a function from elements of $I$ to elements of $M$. Then $v$ is independent on $s$ over $R$, if and only if for all finite sets $t$ of $I$, for all functions $g$ from elements of $I$ to elements of $R$, if $t$ is a subset of $s$, then if for all elements $i_{2}$ of $I$, if $i_{2}$ is not an element of $t$, then $g (i_{2})$ is equal to $0$, then if $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {g (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ is equal to $0$, then for all elements $i$ of $I$, if $i$ is an element of $t$, then $g (i)$ is equal to $0$.

Soit $v$ une fonction des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $M$. Alors $v$ est indépendant sur $s$ sur $R$ si et seulement si pour tous les ensembles finis $t$ de $I$, pour toutes les fonctions $g$ des éléments de $I$ à des éléments de $R$, si $\SetSubsetMACRoFR {t}{s}$, alors si pour tous les éléments $i_{2}$ de $I$, si $i_{2}$ n'est pas un élément de $t$, alors $g (i_{2})$ est égal à $0$, alors si $\FinsetSum {t}{i_{1}}{(\HSMulhSMulMACRoEI {g (i_{1})}{v (i_{1})})}$ est égal à $0$, alors pour tous les éléments $i$ de $I$, si $i$ est un élément de $t$, alors $g (i)$ est égal à $0$.

declarations.doc:
The determinant of a matrix given by the Leibniz formula.

This is available in bundled forms as:
* `Matrix.detMonoidHom`
* `Matrix.detRowAlternating`
declarations.statement: {n : Type u_2} → [DecidableEq n] → [Fintype n] → {R : Type v} → [CommRing R] → Matrix n n R → R
declarations.dedukti:
def Matrix__det : (n : Set) -> (R : Set) -> (M : (Matrix n n R)) -> Elem R :=
  n => R => M => Matrix__detRowAlternating__app M.

readings.Eng: Let $n$ and $R$ be sets. Let $M$ be a matrix of $n$ and $R$. Then the determinant of $n$ is an element of $R$ defined as $\mathrm{Matrix\_\_detRowAlternating\_\_app} (M)$.

\hspace*{1.5em}Soit $x \in n$ tel que il n'est pas le cas que $\EqtMACRoDG {S (x)}{\mathrm{OfNat\_\_ofNat\_\_app} (1 , x)}$.
\hspace*{1.5em}Il suffit de montrer que $\EqtMACRoDG {\FinsetProd {\FinsetunivMACRoEG}{i}{\mathrm{Matrix\_\_diagonal} (d , S (i), i)}}{0}$.

declarations.doc: If you add multiples of row `B k` to other rows, the determinant doesn't change.
declarations.statement:
∀ {n : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] {R : Type v} [inst_2 : CommRing R] {A B : Matrix n n R}
  (c : n → R) (k : n), c k = 0 → (∀ (i j : n), A i j = B i j + c i * B k j) → A.det = B.det
declarations.dedukti: Matrix__det_eq_of_forall_row_eq_smul_add_const : (n : Set) -> (_ : Proof (Fintype n)) -> (R : Set) -> (_ : Proof (CommRing R)) -> (A : (Matrix n n R)) -> (B : (Matrix n n R)) -> (c : (Elem n -> R)) -> (k : Elem n) -> (hk : Proof (Eqt R (c k) 0)) -> (A_eq : Proof (forall n (i => forall n (j => Eqt R (A i j) (plus (B i j) (times (c i) (B k j))))))) -> Proof (Eqt R (Matrix__det n R A) (Matrix__det n R B)).

readings.Eng: Let $n$ be a finite type. Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $A$ and $B$ be matrixes of $n$ and $R$. Let $c$ be a function from elements of $n$ to elements of $R$. Let $k \in n$ such that $c (k)$ is equal to $0$ and for all elements $i$ and $j$ of $n$, $A (i , j)$ is equal to $B (i , j)+ c (i)\times B (k , j)$. Then the determinant of $A$ is equal to the determinant of $B$.
readings.Fre: Soit $n$ un type fini. Soit $R$ un anneau commutatif. Soient $A$ et $B$ des matrices de $n$ et $R$. Soit $c$ une fonction des éléments de $n$ à des éléments de $R$. Soit $k \in n$ tel que $c (k)$ est égal à $0$ et pour tous les éléments $i$ et $j$ de $n$, $A (i , j)$ est égal à $B (i , j)+ c (i)\times B (k , j)$. Alors le déterminant de $A$ est égal au déterminant de $B$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $n$ je konečný typ. Nechť $R$ je komutativní okruh. Nechť $A$ a $B$ je matice $n$ a $R$. Nechť $c$ je funkce z prvků z $n$ do prvků z $R$. Nechť $k \in n$ takový, že $c (k)$ je rovné $0$ a pro všechny prvky $i$ a $j$ z $n$, $A (i , j)$ je rovné $B (i , j)+ c (i)\times B (k , j)$. Tedy determinant $A$ je rovný determinantu $B$.

declarations.doc:
The determinant of a 2×2 block matrix with the lower-left block equal to zero is the product of
the determinants of the diagonal blocks. For the generalization to any number of blocks, see
`Matrix.det_of_isUpperTriangular`.

The determinant of a 2×2 block matrix with the upper-right block equal to zero is the product of
the determinants of the diagonal blocks. For the generalization to any number of blocks, see
`Matrix.det_of_isLowerTriangular`.

∀ {R : Type v} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R),

readings.Eng: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $n \in \Natural$. Let $A$ be a matrix of $\FinMACRoHJ {\mathrm{succ} (n)}$ and $R$. Then the determinant of $A$ is equal to $\FinsetSum {\FinsetunivMACRoDZ}{j}{(\NegnegMACRoFV {1}^ {j}\times A (0 , j)\times \MatrixdetMACRoGY {\mathrm{Matrix\_\_submatrix} (A , \mathrm{Fin\_\_succ} , \mathrm{Fin\_\_succAbove} (j))})}$.
readings.Fre: Soit $R$ un anneau commutatif. Soit $n \in \Natural$. Soit $A$ une matrice de $\FinMACRoHJ {\mathrm{succ} (n)}$ et $R$. Alors le déterminant de $A$ est égal à $\FinsetSum {\FinsetunivMACRoDZ}{j}{(\NegnegMACRoFV {1}^ {j}\times A (0 , j)\times \MatrixdetMACRoGY {\mathrm{Matrix\_\_submatrix} (A , \mathrm{Fin\_\_succ} , \mathrm{Fin\_\_succAbove} (j))})}$.

declarations.doc:
A (left) ideal in a semiring `R` is an additive submonoid `s` such that
`a * b ∈ s` whenever `b ∈ s`. If `R` is a ring, then `s` is an additive subgroup.
declarations.statement: (R : Type u) → [Semiring R] → Type u
declarations.dedukti:
def Ideal : (R : Set) -> Set :=
  R => Submodule R R.

readings.Eng: Let $R$ be a set. Then an ideal of $R$ is an element of the function that maps $R$ to the set of submodules of $R$ over $R$.
readings.Fre: Soit $R$ un ensemble. Alors un idéal de $R$ est un élément de la fonction qui envoie $R$ sur l'ensemble de sous-modules de $R$ sur $R$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $R$ je množina. Tedy ideál $R$ je prvek z funkce která zobrazuje $R$ na množinu podmodulů $R$ nad $R$.

declarations.doc: A left ideal `I : Ideal R` is two-sided if it is also a right ideal.
declarations.statement: {α : Type u} → [inst : Semiring α] → Ideal α → Prop
declarations.dedukti: Ideal__IsTwoSided : (X : Set) -> (I : Elem (Ideal X)) -> Prop.

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an ideal of $X$. Then we can say that $X$ is two-sided.
readings.Fre: Soit $X$ un ensemble. Soit $I$ un idéal de $X$. Alors nous pouvons dire que $X$ est bilatère.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ je množina. Nechť $I$ je ideál $X$. Tedy můžeme říkat, že $X$ je oboustranné.

declarations.statement: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Semiring α] {I : Ideal α}, (∀ {a : α} (b : α), a ∈ I → a * b ∈ I) → I.IsTwoSided
declarations.dedukti: Ideal__IsTwoSided__mk : (X : Set) -> (_ : Proof (Semiring X)) -> (I : Elem (Ideal X)) -> (mul_mem_of_left : Proof (forall X (a => forall X (b => if (Membership__mem X (Ideal X) I a) (Membership__mem X (Ideal X) I (times a b)))))) -> Proof (Ideal__IsTwoSided X I).

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a semiring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $X$ such that for all elements $a$ and $b$ of $X$, if $a$ is an element of $I$, then $a \times b$ is an element of $I$. Then $I$ is two-sided.
readings.Fre: Soit $X$ un semi-anneau. Soit $I$ un idéal de $X$ tel que pour tous les éléments $a$ et $b$ de $X$, si $a$ est un élément de $I$, alors $a \times b$ soit un élément de $I$. Alors $I$ est bilatère.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ je polookruh. Nechť $I$ je ideál $X$ takový, že pro všechny prvky $a$ a $b$ z $X$, jestliže $a$ je element $I$, pak $a \times b$ je element $I$. Tedy $I$ je oboustranné.
readings.formula: $X \in \mathrm{Set} , [AppPredicateFormula] , I \in \mathrm{Ideal} (X), \forall a \in X . \forall b \in X . \MembershipmemMACRoDX {I}{a}\rightarrow \MembershipmemMACRoDX {I}{a \times b}\vdash [AppPredicateFormula]$

declarations.statement: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Semiring α] (I : Ideal α), I.IsTwoSided ↔ ∀ {a : α} (b : α), a ∈ I → a * b ∈ I
declarations.dedukti: Ideal__isTwoSided_iff : (X : Set) -> (_ : Proof (Semiring X)) -> (I : Elem (Ideal X)) -> Proof (iff (Ideal__IsTwoSided X I) (forall X (a => forall X (b => if (Membership__mem X (Ideal X) I a) (Membership__mem X (Ideal X) I (times a b)))))).

readings.Eng: Let $X$ be a semiring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $X$. Then $I$ is two-sided, if and only if for all elements $a$ and $b$ of $X$, if $a$ is an element of $I$, then $a \times b$ is an element of $I$.
readings.Fre: Soit $X$ un semi-anneau. Soit $I$ un idéal de $X$. Alors $I$ est bilatère si et seulement si pour tous les éléments $a$ et $b$ de $X$, si $a$ est un élément de $I$, alors $a \times b$ est un élément de $I$.
readings.Cze: Nechť $X$ je polookruh. Nechť $I$ je ideál $X$. Tedy $I$ je oboustranné, právě tehdy, když pro všechny prvky $a$ a $b$ z $X$, jestliže $a$ je element $I$, pak $a \times b$ je element $I$.
